references.text: Abraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, old and satisfied with life, and was gathered to his people - the same wording is used for Isaac's death.
Ishmael's death is described with almost identical wording: he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people.
Jacob asked to be gathered to his fathers and buried in the family tomb, paralleling Isaac's death and gathering to his people.
The immediate context: Isaac lived in Mamre and reached 180 years of age, which introduces the account of his death.
Esau had planned to kill Jacob after Isaac's death, but here the two brothers bury their father together in reconciliation.
Joseph's death and his command that his bones be taken out of Egypt, as part of the patriarchs' final destiny.
The verse confirms that Isaac was buried with his fathers, which underscores the continuity of God's promise regarding the land.
The identical death formula for Jacob creates a theological symmetry and confirms that all three patriarchs completed their calling.
